analysis.title: Early Morning Reid: October 2026 Performance Review
key_insights: October was volatile: AI-trade doubts, French sovereign stress and US-Iran tensions pushing energy higher. Brent rose 13.6% and European natural gas rose above €100/MWh for the first time since 2022.

Treasuries returned +2.3% in October, their best month of 2026, after the US 10yr hit a post-2002 high of 5.31% early in the month. The 10yr ended at 4.93% as risk sentiment worsened and the Fed, ECB and BoJ all held rates.
The Nasdaq fell 5.3%, its worst month since March 2025, on AI capex return concerns. Intel fell 45% and CoreWeave 37%. The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 19% between October 6 and month-end.

Alphabet fell 12.64% after its results, its worst day on record, as investors scrutinised hyperscaler capex plans. Alphabet (-18.7%) and Meta (-15.2%) were notable single-name underperformers after disappointing Q3 results.
The tech sell-off masked rotation under the surface. The S&P 500 lost 0.9% while the equal-weighted version gained 5.0%, reversing its September decline.

France was at the centre of European sovereign stress. The 10yr OAT-Bund spread reached 174bps on October 22, its highest since November 2011, and the French 10yr yield hit a post-2002 high of 5.07%. Stress spilled into Italian and Spanish spreads, European banks and the euro.

The EURO STOXX Banks index had its worst total return month since 2023 (-11.4%). European HY spreads widened 65bps to 370bps, the biggest monthly widening since 2022. The euro ended the month at 1.1160, its lowest against the dollar since spring 2025.

Brent ended October at $117.64/bbl, near its 2026 high, with a YTD gain of +93.3%. Drivers were Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, and reports the US may resume strikes on Iran after the November 2 midterms.

Emerging markets: MSCI EM fell 8.0%, its worst month since March. Brazil's Bovespa fell 9.9% in local currency (14.3% in USD) after Lula's surprise election win on October 25. Shanghai Composite fell 6.1% despite Q3 GDP of +4.5% y/y.
Gold fell 6.8% and silver 18.7%, to their lowest levels since October and November 2025 respectively.
KOSPI fell 16.2%, the weakest country index globally, and the Nikkei fell 5.2%, both under AI-related pressure.
September US CPI rose 0.65% headline and 0.33% core, yet Treasuries rallied. Fed, ECB and BoJ holds left markets less convinced that the previously priced tightening will materialise.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Strong inflation data did not stop Treasuries from rallying in October.
Core inflation was firm, but the Fed's hold left markets less convinced that the priced tightening will happen.
Stronger growth was offset by soft domestic demand and the global tech sell-off, and the Shanghai Composite still fell 6.1%.

risk_factors: AI capex return doubts spreading from semiconductors to hyperscalers.
US-Iran military re-escalation after the November 2 midterms.
French sovereign and political stress spilling into periphery spreads, European banks and the euro.
Continued disruption to Middle East energy flows and high European gas prices.
EM risk-off from higher oil and the Brazilian election outcome.
geopolitical: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and grey shipping disruption through the Strait of Hormuz kept oil supply tight.
Reports that the US administration may resume military strikes against Iran after the November 2 midterm elections added a risk premium to oil.
Renewed political unrest in France pushed the OAT-Bund spread to its widest since 2011.
Lula's surprise Brazilian presidential election win on October 25 triggered a sharp Bovespa sell-off.
